title: Cohomological delta-functors, their morphisms, and universal delta-functors
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. A *(cohomological) $\delta$-functor* $F=(F^n,\delta_F)$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ consists of (a) additive functors $F^n:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $n\ge0$, and (b) for every short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$, morphisms $\delta_{F,A\to B\to C}^n:F^n(C)\to F^{n+1}(A)$, $n\ge0$, such that (1) for every short exact sequence the sequence $0\to F^0(A)\xrightarrow{F^0(f)}F^0(B)\xrightarrow{F^0(g)}F^0(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}F^1(A)\xrightarrow{F^1(f)}F^1(B)\to\cdots\to F^n(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^n}F^{n+1}(A)\to\cdots$ is exact, and (2) for every morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences from $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ to $0\to A'\to B'\to C'\to0$ (morphisms $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $c:C\to C'$ commuting with the maps of the sequences) one has $F^{n+1}(a)\circ\delta^n_{F,A\to B\to C}=\delta^n_{F,A'\to B'\to C'}\circ F^n(c)$ for all $n\ge0$. A *morphism of $\delta$-functors* $F\to G$ is a family of natural transformations $t^n:F^n\to G^n$, $n\ge0$, such that $t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,A\to B\to C}=\delta^n_{G,A\to B\to C}\circ t^n_C$ for every short exact sequence and every $n\ge0$. A $\delta$-functor $F$ is *universal* if for every $\delta$-functor $G$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ and every natural transformation $t:F^0\to G^0$ there is a unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $(t^n)_{n\ge0}:F\to G$ with $t^0=t$.
